1. Summary of the primary business
a. Business Overview - Products and Services
As per the CRISIL Report, we are a manufacturer of multiple grades of custom formulated polymer
compounds. Polymer compounds are used as an essential raw material for sheathing, jacketing and insulation
of wires and cables as well as coating of underground oil, gas and water pipelines. Our product portfolio is
well diversified to offer varied solutions in the wire and cables and infrastructure industry. For more details,
please refer to “Our Business” on page 247 of the Red Herring Prospectus.
b. Industries Served / Typical Customers and revenue from operations from key customers:
We serve the telecommunication, power, railway, water distribution and oil and gas distribution industries. 
Our customers are primarily wire and cable manufacturers and pipeline-coating companies in India and, to a 
lesser extent, overseas. We sell predominantly to private customers, largely through direct sales, and a 
significant majority of our revenue comes from repeat customers with whom we have long-standing 
relationships.

c. Segment Reporting and Revenue Contribution
Our Company is primarily engaged in the manufacture and sale of custom-formulated polymer compounds for
wires and cables and industrial pipeline coatings, serving customers in India and overseas. Accordingly, our
Company has one reportable operating segment under Ind AS 108, “Operating Segments”.
d. Key Geographies
During the three month period ended June 30, 2026 and the Financial Years ended March 31, 2026, March 31, 
2025 and March 31, 2024, our operations were spread across 23 states/union territories. We have also 
established an international market presence by exporting to countries such as, Bangladesh, Egypt, Oman, 
Saudi Arabia, Turkey, United Arab Emirates, United States of America and Zambia. During the three months 
period ended June 30, 2026 and the preceding three Fiscals, we served customers across 13 countries. 
e. Key Manufacturing Facilities
We primarily operate through nine Operating Facilities, comprising one manufacturing facility and one 
warehouse in Goa, two warehouses in New Delhi, and one godown in Bhiwandi.

2. Summary of the Industry (Source: CRISIL Report)
The Indian polymer compounding market increased from approximately USD 5,967 million in 2019 to USD 
9,934 million in 2025 and is expected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 9.0% during 2026–2031, reaching

3
approximately USD 16,507 million by 2031. Growth is supported by industrialisation, infrastructure 
development, power sector expansion, renewable energy integration, telecommunications expansion, 
urbanisation and increasing adoption of lightweight and high-performance materials. The Indian polymer 
compounding industry is a specialised segment of the polymer industry involving the combination of base 
polymers with additives, fillers and reinforcements to develop materials with application-specific performance
characteristics. The industry caters to diverse end-use sectors including automotive, construction and 
infrastructure, electrical and electronics, telecommunications, agriculture, wires and cables, and oil, gas and 
water pipeline infrastructure.
For further information, see “Industry Overview” beginning on page 160 of the Red Herring Prospectus.

4. Net asset value (NAV) per equity share* (₹): Net worth excluding minority interest as restated at the end of the year

5. Profit Before Tax is calculated as Total Income Less Total Expenses.
6. Net worth’ means the aggregate value of the paid-up share capital and all reserves created out of the profits and

value of the accumulated losses, deferred expenditure and miscellaneous expenditure not written off, but does not
include reserves created out of revaluation of assets, write-back of depreciation and amalgamation.
7. Revenue from Operations is calculated as revenue recognized from the Company's core business activities.
8. Total Income is calculated as Revenue from Operations plus Other Income.
9. EBITDA is calculated as Profit Before Tax plus Interest Expense plus Depreciation and Amortization less Other
Income.
10. EBIT is calculated as Profit Before Tax plus Interest Expense.
11. PAT is calculated as Profit Before Tax Less Total Tax Expense.
12. Gross Margin (%) is calculated as (Revenue from Operations less Cost of materials consumed, Purchase of stock￾in-trade and Change in inventories) divided by Revenue from Operations multiplied by 100.
13. EBITDA Margin (%) is calculated as EBITDA divided by Revenue from Operations multiplied by 100.
14. PAT Margin (%) is calculated as PAT divided by Revenue from Operations multiplied by 100.
15. ROE (%) is calculated as PAT attributable to owners divided by Average Total Equity multiplied by 100.
16. ROCE (%) is calculated as EBIT divided by Capital Employed multiplied by 100.

include reserves created out of revaluation of assets, write-back of depreciation and amalgamation.

8. Total Income is calculated as Revenue from Operations plus Other Income.
9. EBITDA is calculated as Profit Before Tax plus Interest Expense plus Depreciation and Amortization less Other
Income.
10. EBIT is calculated as Profit Before Tax plus Interest Expense.
11. PAT is calculated as Profit Before Tax Less Total Tax Expense.
12. Gross Margin (%) is calculated as (Revenue from Operations less Cost of materials consumed, Purchase of stock￾in-trade and Change in inventories) divided by Revenue from Operations multiplied by 100.
13. EBITDA Margin (%) is calculated as EBITDA divided by Revenue from Operations multiplied by 100.
14. PAT Margin (%) is calculated as PAT divided by Revenue from Operations multiplied by 100.
15. ROE (%) is calculated as PAT attributable to owners divided by Average Total Equity multiplied by 100.
16. ROCE (%) is calculated as EBIT divided by Capital Employed multiplied by 100.
